title: Runtime: add H100 attention kernel variant v3 + fallback rules; export kernel_choice metric
author: Grace Kim
release_notes:
- H100-only: new attention kernel variant v3 enabled via profile selection (auto) with conservative fallbacks
- New metric: runtime_kernel_choice (tagged by profile_id, sku, model_family) to debug kernel selection and unexpected fallbacks
commits: runtime(attn): introduce h100_attn_v3 kernel wrapper + capability checks
runtime(attn): selection policy: prefer v3; fallback to v2 on unsupported shapes / dtype / cuda / driver
runtime(metrics): export runtime_kernel_choice counter + structured debug log line
tests: add kernel selection unit tests + golden snapshots for H100 capability matrix
bench: add microbench harness integration + perf notes for v3 vs v2
body:
Summary
Adds a new H100 attention kernel variant ("v3") and updates the runtime kernel selection logic to prefer v3 when safe, with deterministic fallbacks to v2 for unsupported/unstable combinations. Also exports a low-cardinality metric to make kernel choice observable in production and benchmark-lab.

Motivation
We currently rely on the v2 H100 attention path for most workloads. Kernel team microbenchmarks show v3 provides better decode TPS at moderate batch/concurrency, but it is more sensitive to shape/dtype/driver/CUDA constraints. We need to ship v3 behind selection rules + telemetry so we can:
- Safely roll it out via the new hardware profile pack (ENG-4925)
- Debug tail latency regressions where we silently fall back to a slower kernel
- Provide on-call a single place to confirm "what kernel are we actually using?"

What changed
1) New kernel variant: h100_attn_v3
- Adds a new kernel wrapper with explicit capability checks
- Supported dtypes: fp16, bf16 (no fp8 in this PR)
- Supported head_dim: 128 only (explicitly rejects others)

2) Selection policy (H100-only)
- Prefer v3 when all of the below are true:
  - GPU: H100 (SM90) detected at runtime
  - CUDA runtime >= 12.4 AND driver >= 550 (see notes below)
  - dtype in {fp16, bf16}
  - head_dim == 128
  - q_len <= max_prefill_q (defaults: 8k for now; can be bumped via profile)
  - no "force_attention_kernel" override set to v2
- Fallback to v2 with a reason code when any check fails.
- Runtime will log the chosen kernel once per model-load and will also emit per-request counters (sampled) to avoid log spam.

3) Fallback rules (deterministic + observable)
- v3 -> v2 fallback reasons (enumerated):
  - unsupported_dtype
  - unsupported_head_dim
  - cuda_or_driver_too_old
  - q_len_too_large
  - kernel_launch_failed (rare; guarded with one retry + immediate downgrade)
- kernel_launch_failed triggers:
  - A single retry on v2 for the same request (to avoid hard failing user traffic)
  - A sticky downgrade for the model instance for 10 minutes (configurable) to prevent flapping

4) New metric: runtime_kernel_choice
- Counter with tags:
  - sku (e.g., "H100-SXM", "H100-PCIe" as available)
  - kernel ("h100_attn_v2" | "h100_attn_v3" | "other")
  - model_family (coarsened; e.g., "llama", "mistral", "qwen")
  - profile_id (from profile pack)
  - reason (only set when kernel != preferred; small enum)
- Metric name chosen to be compatible with our existing metrics registry + avoid high-cardinality labels.

Perf results (microbench)
All numbers are from benchmark/microbench/attention_microbench on H100-SXM (CUDA 12.4, driver 550.54), bf16.
- Decode-heavy (q_len=1, kv=8k, batch=16): v3 +6-9% tokens/sec vs v2
- Mixed (q_len=256, kv=4k, batch=8): v3 +3-5% tokens/sec vs v2
- Long prefill (q_len=16k): v3 is currently disabled (fallback) due to observed variance and occasional launch failures; will revisit once we complete the long-context kernel gate work.

Rollout plan
- This PR only adds the kernel, selection logic, and metrics.
- Enabling is controlled by the profile pack defaults (separate PRs). For now, v3 is "preferred" but gated by conservative shape/driver/CUDA checks.
- SRE note: please add runtime_kernel_choice panels to the Runtime Profiles dashboard (Allison is already tracking on ENG-4931).

Testing
- Unit tests: kernel selection matrix (H100 vs non-H100, supported vs unsupported dtype/head_dim, driver/CUDA gate)
- Added golden snapshot to ensure we don\'t accidentally expand v3 to unsupported head_dims
- Manually tested on:
  - H100-SXM: v3 selected for supported shapes; metric increments as expected
  - L40S: never selects v3; metric shows other/v2 as appropriate

Notes / follow-ups
- FP8 path intentionally excluded to keep scope small; we\'ll add once we confirm stability + correct scaling semantics.
- Long-context support: we should either (a) raise the q_len gate once stable, or (b) add a separate long-context variant with explicit compatibility checks. Tracking in ENG-4925 comments.

References
- Linear: ENG-4925 (Kernel tuning: H100 attention kernel variant selection + fallback rules)
- Linear: ENG-4931 (Observability additions: add runtime tags/counters)
- Related scheduler work: ENG-4924 (mixed workload buckets) — kernel fallback visibility helps distinguish queueing vs compute regressions.
conversation:
Hiro Tanaka (reviewer): Can you clarify why the CUDA/driver gate is hardcoded to 12.4/550? Is this coming from a specific compiler feature or observed instability?
Grace Kim (author): Observed instability. v3 uses a codepath that reliably compiles/launches on 12.4+ in our lab images. On 12.2 we saw sporadic launch failures under higher concurrency. I added the gate to be conservative until Infra finishes standardizing images; we can relax later with additional CI coverage.

Yuki Sato (reviewer): The q_len <= 8k gate seems arbitrary. Do we have data for 12k/16k? Also: the "sticky downgrade" timer is new behavior; can we make it visible in logs/metrics?
Grace Kim (author): Agree it\'s conservative. We have some 16k prefill runs showing variance and occasional failures; no stable 12k set yet. I added a TODO + made max_prefill_q a profile knob so we can bump after more benchmark-lab coverage. For sticky downgrade, I added reason=kernel_launch_failed and a log line when the downgrade is activated (once per model instance).

Noah Patel (reviewer): Metric tags: please ensure model_family is coarsened and not raw model_id. Also check cardinality of profile_id (it\'s versioned but still bounded).
Grace Kim (author): Done. model_family comes from the existing coarse classifier (llama/mistral/qwen/other). profile_id is already a small enum in the profile pack; I used that field rather than full profile_version+hash.

Allison Grant (reviewer): Naming: can we align with existing metrics naming (runtime_*). Also, can you add a counter for fallback reason only when we expected v3 but got v2?
Grace Kim (author): Renamed to runtime_kernel_choice. The reason label is only set on non-preferred selection (e.g., preferred=v3 but chosen=v2). When v2 is preferred by config override, reason stays empty to avoid confusion.

Hiro Tanaka (reviewer): One more: kernel_launch_failed -> retry on v2 is good, but do we risk masking actual correctness issues? Any correctness validation?
Grace Kim (author): The retry is only to avoid failing user traffic; errors still increment runtime_kernel_choice with reason=kernel_launch_failed and we log the CUDA error string. Correctness-wise, the kernel is the same math as v2; I also ran the existing attention correctness suite locally and it passed. We can add a targeted regression test in a follow-up if you want it in-tree.

Hiro Tanaka (reviewer): LGTM after the minor nits (comment about why q_len is gated + one more unit test for override precedence).
Grace Kim (author): Addressed: added comment and a test case where force_attention_kernel=v2 forces v2 even when v3 would be allowed.
Allison Grant (reviewer): Approved (please ping me when this is in a build so we can wire the dashboard panel).
